features.optics-sfp-plus: the two Virtual Chassis ports and the two uplink ports are 1GE or 10GE SFP+ ports (Table 9 and Figure 3 callout 10). Virtual Chassis is supported only with 10GE SFP+, and not with a 10GBASE-T transceiver in a Virtual Chassis port. Industrial-grade optics are required above 35 C for under-the-desk mounting and above 40 C otherwise
features.uplink-ports: two SFP+ ports take 1 GbE or 10 GbE transceivers
features.virtual-chassis: up to 6 EX4000 switches; the two Virtual Chassis ports are SFP+ and VC formation is not supported with a 10GBASE-T transceiver in them

management.usb: one USB 2.0 Type-A port on the front panel

configs.description: The switch as shipped: 12 non-PoE ports, the built-in AC power supply and no fan. EX4000-12T is the only hardware SKU the datasheet lists for the model (Table 1 and the ordering information); there is no DC, -S or -TAA variant.
configs.name: ac

gaps.wanted: The brackets of EX4000-2PST-RMK (the two-post rack kit, orderable, Table 5) are named in the mounting topics and are not modelled as a kit contract in this slice. A dimensioned drawing of the bracket fold lines would give the switch ear positions; none is stated here.

A per-port vocabulary for the Status lamp. Table 32 gives its colour by speed (off 10 Mbps, blinking green 100 Mbps, green 1000 Mbps, amber 2.5 Gbps), which the jack's own lamp states do not carry, so the jack keeps the component's default off, link and activity states.
The size of the claim code label (Figure 3 callout 6). It is drawn as a region and not as a part, and the photograph does not show it.
The Junos interface names. The hardware guide gives the PIC numbering only inside the Junos configuration topics, which this slice does not read.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.
The diameter and depth of the pinhole reset button (Figure 3 callout 7). The guide names the button and gives no size; the hole is drawn at 2.0 mm as an estimate.
an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on port group rj45 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: Table 8 and the cooling section - natural convection, no fan; the datasheet gives no airflow. The guide says not to block the vents on top of the switch.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Table 8 and Table 9 - the switch has an internal power supply (fixed PSU) and no fan (natural convection cooling, fan-less switch); the guide's system overview says the EX4000 switch models have inbuilt fixed power supply units. The guide gives no replacement procedure and no part number. The supply is part of the chassis and not a bay and not a component.

chassis.note: Table 9 and Table 26 - height 1.75 in (4.44 cm), width 10.39 in (26.40 cm), depth 9.64 in (24.5 cm), weight 5.07 lb (2.30 kg). The datasheet gives the same width, a height of 1.71 in (4.34 cm), a depth of 9.57 in (24.3 cm) and a system weight of 2.30 kg. The guide's table is the table of chassis sizes and is carried, so the height is 44.4 mm (the 1U pitch) and the depth 245.0 mm; the photograph's face measures 43.2 mm from the top edge to the lower edge, the rest being the feet and the rounded lower corners, which are not drawn. The unit is 264.0 mm wide, not a rack width: the optional two-post kit EX4000-2PST-RMK (Table 5) carries it in a rack.

color.note: median of the bare face left of the first jack shell in the front photograph, #626e7a, which is darker and bluer than the 1U models'; the rear photograph's metal reads lighter under the same lights. One chassis colour is carried and is the front's. The numerals are the photograph's white, #e4e6e9.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The drawing and the photograph agree on what is on the face. The photograph prints the port numbers in white on this non-PoE model and the drawing in black, and prints only EX4000 as the model legend. The Juniper logo and the driven by Mist AI line are not drawn: a logo-zone is reserved. The rounded corners and the feet of the compact case are not drawn.

earthing.note: The Connect to Power topic and Figure 4 - a two-hole protective earthing terminal on the rear panel, secured with two M5 x 10 mm screws with washers (not supplied) and a lug on 6 AWG wire. The holes are drawn as decor.

front-layout.note: estimated - Figure 3 and the front photograph. The face is the EX4000-12P's: 12 jacks in one shell of six columns and two rows, the first cell at 60.1 mm, the column pitch 13.97 mm, the rows 14.3 mm apart with the upper row turned 180 so that its latch and lamps face up; four SFP+ cages abut on the registry's 14.25 mm pitch from 152.2 mm, each with a small lamp either side of its number; the RJ-45 management port stands over the USB 2.0 Type-A port in one housing and the console port in its own; the status pill is at the top right and the reset pinhole at the right end. Checked against the photograph by overlay.

guide-faces.note: The guide has flat drawings of the front (Figure 3) and rear (Figure 4) and no top, bottom or side elevations; the isometric views are not used.

mounting.note: Table 5 and the mounting topics - on a desk by default (the quick-start topic), and with the orderable kits EX4000-2PST-RMK (two-post rack), EX4000-WMK (wall or under a desk), EX4000-MMK (magnet pads), EX4000-DRK (DIN rail) and the cable guard EX4000-12-CGD. No figure measures a bracket fold line, so no ear position and no kit is listed here: they are named in this provenance and are not modelled as kind kit contracts. A rack needs 2RU of clearance above the unit.

port-lamps.note: Figures 22 to 25 and Tables 32 and 33 - each RJ-45 jack has a Link Activity lamp at one corner and a Status lamp at the other; the common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 housing carries both. Each SFP+ port has a Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp, the small bars either side of its number (Figure 25). Which bar is which lamp is not stated, so the left bar is taken as Link Activity by analogy with the jacks and is estimated. The Status lamp's colour shows speed (Table 32), so its states are not expressible as one vocabulary here (see gaps).

port-numbering.note: The photograph and Figure 3 print 0 and 1, 2 and 3, up to 10 and 11 under the column pairs, each number followed by its triangle (an up triangle after the even number and a down triangle after the odd one), so the upper jack of a column is the even port. The numbers are white on this non-PoE model, orange on the PoE models. The four SFP+ cages are printed 0, 1, 2 and 3, with 0 and 1 inside a rounded outline: the Virtual Chassis ports are 0 and 1 and the uplink ports 2 and 3 (Figure 3 callout 10). Port numbers are as printed on the metal, from 0. The guide gives no interface names, so none is recorded.

power.note: Table 34 - input 100 to 240 VAC at 0.9 A, 50 to 60 Hz. The datasheet's Table 2 gives a maximum system power consumption of 34 W with no PoE. The guide's PoE budget table (Table 35) has no row for the non-PoE models. The cord is a C13 coupler (power cord topic).

rear.note: estimated - Figure 4 and the rear photograph at 6.556 px/mm. From the left: a round hole for the power cord retainer (callout 1), the AC inlet in a black housing with its rating printed under it (callout 2), three screw heads along the lower edge and the two-hole protective earthing terminal on a lighter plate with the earth symbol under it (callout 3). Unlike the EX4000-12P there is no heat-sink vent and no hot-surface triangle.

scale.note: Gate 1 on the front photograph (2100 x 729 px): the body runs from 184 to 1912 px, 6.55 px/mm against the 264.0 mm width, and the jack-label pitch reads the registry's 13.97 mm ganged pitch to within a percent. The guide's flat drawing (Figure 3) was used for what is on the face and for the callouts. The rear photograph (2100 x 720 px) runs from 179 to 1910 px and reads at 6.556 px/mm.

sources.note: EX4000 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2026-01-20 (261 pages; PDF created 2026-01-20; fetched from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4000/ex4000.pdf, which answered): Table 3 (models), Figure 3 and Figure 4 (the EX4000-12T front and rear panels, flat drawings), Tables 8 and 9 (cooling, power and the physical specifications and ports), Table 26 (chassis), Tables 27 to 33 (the lamps), Table 34 (input), Table 5 (mounting kits) and the mounting topics. EX4000 Line of Ethernet Switches Datasheet, Juniper Networks (PDF created 2025-05-28, 14 pages; https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex4000-line-of-ethernet-switches-datasheet.pdf): Table 1 (the SKUs), Table 2 (maximum system power without PoE), the specifications and the ordering information. Juniper's image-library photographs ex4000-12t-front-high.jpg and ex4000-12t-rear-high.jpg (from https://www.juniper.net/us/en/company/images/image-library-logos-and-product-photos/products/ex4000-12t.html, 2100 px wide, straight on). The guide prints no terms of use; the image-library page prints none either. Nothing of any of them is copied here, since every face is drawn new from measurements. No Visio stencil and no 3D model of the EX4000 is held or published; the intake folder for Juniper EX and QFX was not available to this work and no held photograph, stencil or model was used. End of life was searched on 2026-10-23 and no Juniper notice for the EX4000 was found, so the lifecycle is recorded as none announced.

status-block.note: estimated - Figure 3 callouts 3, 4 and 5 and the photograph. The three chassis lamps SYS, MST and CLD sit in a rounded pill at the top right with a round lamp before each legend, as the photograph and the drawing show. Tables 27 to 30 give the lamp meanings; the CLD blink patterns are in another document and are not stated here.

usb-reset.note: estimated - Figure 3 callouts 6, 7 and 9. The USB 2.0 Type-A port under the management port, the reset pinhole (callout 7, with the reset symbol below) and the claim code label (callout 6, a QR code at the right of the drawing and absent from the photograph, so a region and not a part) are read off the figure and the photograph.
